bugLogs.title: Insufficient color contrast for error message text
steps_to_reproduce: 1. Navigate to the checkout page where the credit‑card input is located.
2. Submit the form with an invalid card number to trigger the error message.
3. Observe the paragraph with id="card-error" displaying the text "Please enter a valid card number".
4. Use a contrast‑checking tool (e.g., WebAIM Contrast Checker) to measure the contrast between the text color #ff9999 and the page background #ffffff.
bugLogs.expected_behavior: The error message text must have a contrast ratio of at least 4.5:1 against its background, as required by WCAG 2.1 Success Criterion 1.4.3 (Contrast Minimum).
bugLogs.actual_behavior: The text color #ff9999 on a white background #ffffff yields a contrast ratio of 2.04:1, which is below the required 4.5:1 threshold for normal-sized text.

bugLogs.title: Select element missing accessible name
steps_to_reproduce: 1. Open the page containing the <select id="state"> element.
2. Navigate to the select control using only the keyboard (Tab key).
3. Activate a screen reader (e.g., NVDA, VoiceOver) and listen for the announced label of the control.
4. Observe that the control is announced without a name (e.g., "select, collapsed"), providing no context.
bugLogs.expected_behavior: The select control must have an accessible name that can be programmatically determined, such as a visible <label> associated via for/id, an aria-label, aria-labelledby, or a title attribute, so screen readers announce a meaningful name (e.g., "State").
bugLogs.actual_behavior: The <select id="state"> element has no associated <label>, no aria-label, no aria-labelledby, and no title attribute, resulting in no accessible name being announced.
bugLogs.suggested_fix:
Add a visible label linked to the select, or provide an ARIA label. Example fix:
html
<label for="state">State</label>
<select id="state" name="state" aria-label="State">
  <option value="">Select State</option>
  <option value="CA">California</option>
  <option value="NY">New York</option>
  <option value="TX">Texas</option>
</select>
